body:
Written by Claude Opus 5.5 via Claude Code for the Olares maintainers; I prompted it, it did the work, I read it.

**Environment:** Olares 1.12.6, single node (Olares One), `mongodb` and `mysql` system middleware installed from the Market.

**Summary:** the MongoDB and MySQL middlewares filled their local PVs with logs, about 100 GB between them, while holding almost no data. Nothing in Olares surfaces this; it only shows up as disk usage under `/var/openebs/local/pvc-*`. Almost all of the logged traffic comes from KubeBlocks' own sidecars in the pod, not from apps.

**MySQL (`mysql-middleware/mysql-mysql-0`, MySQL 8.0.39)**
- `general_log=ON`, `general_log_file=/var/lib/mysql/log/mysqld.log`
- One unrotated file, 29 GB, written continuously since the pod was created (2026-04-02).
- Content is almost entirely `kbagent` probes, about 10 statements per second-interval probe: `select check_ts from kubeblocks.kb_health_check …`, `show replica status`, `select @@global.rpl_semi_sync_source_enabled`, etc.
- The instance had no consumers: no MiddlewareRequest referenced mysql, and the only non-system schema was `kubeblocks`.

**MongoDB (`mongodb-middleware/mongodb-mongodb-0`)**
- `logs/` on the PV held 73 GB across 23 rotated `mongodb.log.<timestamp>` files going back to 2026-03-07; data (`db/`) was 1.2 GB. Rotation happens, but old files are never deleted. Single files reached 24 GB (rotated 2026-05-30) and 13 GB (2026-08-06).
- In the last ~40 h of log, all ~28k connections came from inside the pod: `mongo-go-driver` with appName `pbm-agent` (8.4k), `mongo-go-driver` with no appName from 127.0.0.1 (12k) and from the pod IP (8.1k). The agent attributed the unnamed clients to KubeBlocks probes but did not confirm it. Each connection logs accept / client metadata / end.
- The replica set was also unhealthy: `replSetGetStatus` returned "Our replica set config is invalid or we are not a member of it". The stored member host was `mongodb-mongodb-0.mongodb-mongodb-headless.mongodb-middleware.svc:27017`, while `MONGODB_POD_FQDN_LIST` is `…svc.cluster.local`. Whether that mismatch is the cause was not verified. The resulting retry churn plausibly accelerates the log growth.
- The only consumer was Otmoic (`otmoiclp-mongodb` MiddlewareRequest), which had been suspended for 200 days.

**Expected**
- `general_log` off by default for the MySQL middleware, or at least rotated.
- A retention limit on MongoDB's rotated logs (count or size).
- Ideally, health probes that don't produce a log line per probe at the default verbosity.

**Workaround used:** uninstalling both middlewares with `--delete-data`, which was possible only because nothing depended on them.

comments.body: It looks like the logs for both MongoDB and MySQL are growing uncontrollably, filling up disk space. I'd check why the MySQL `general_log` is on by default and why MongoDB's old logs aren't being deleted.

@[user] 
Thanks for report.
You can manually disable these logs.

- MySQL
Disable the MySQL general log (applied dynamically without restarting MySQL):
```
kubectl apply -f - <<'EOF'
apiVersion: operations.kubeblocks.io/v1alpha1
kind: OpsRequest
metadata:
  name: mysql-general-log-off
  namespace: mysql-middleware
spec:
  clusterName: mysql
  type: Reconfiguring
  reconfigures:
  - componentName: mysql
    parameters:
    - key: general_log
      value: "OFF"
EOF
```
And then you can also delete mysqld.log and restart the Pod.

- MongoDB
Reduce MongoDB logging:

Some log messages still cannot be disabled. client metadata (id: 51800) ignores systemLog.quiet on this MongoDB version; that was fixed in MongoDB 8.0 ([SERVER-29109](https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-29109)).

```
kubectl apply -f - <<'EOF'
apiVersion: operations.kubeblocks.io/v1alpha1
kind: OpsRequest
metadata:
  name: mongodb-quiet-log
  namespace: mongodb-middleware
spec:
  clusterName: mongodb
  type: Reconfiguring
  reconfigures:
  - componentName: mongodb
    parameters:
    - key: systemLog.quiet
      value: "true"
EOF
```
systemLog.quiet is a static setting. It takes effect only after the OpsRequest succeeds and mongod restarts. On a single-node deployment, MongoDB will be temporarily unavailable during the restart.

Check the result with:
```
kubectl get opsrequest -n mongodb-middleware mongodb-quiet-log

kubectl exec -n mongodb-middleware mongodb-mongodb-0 -c mongodb -- \
  grep -A6 '^systemLog:' /etc/mongodb/mongodb.conf
```
And then you can also delete mongodb.log.<timestamp> manually.
for my own system i uninstalled the databases, i created this issue so you can resolve this for users that keep using them
@[user] thanks for the workaround. Would you be open to turning general_log off by default and cleaning up the rotated MongoDB logs, so new installs don't fill up the disk?
@[user] In the next version, newly installed MySQL defaults to general_log=OFF, and newly installed MongoDB defaults to systemLog.quiet=true.

title: KubeBlocks MongoDB/MySQL middleware logs grow without bound (MySQL general_log on, rotated MongoDB logs never deleted)
